- Or, alternatively, can you provide a small credit top-up (token credit) we can draw against while we finish the integration?

Hi Sara — thanks for the note and for calling out the schema snag. We can support both paths; below are two options we typically offer for this exact situation (keeps you in the same sandbox and avoids re-setup):

Option A — Short time extension (time-stretch)
- 3-week extension to current pilot term
- Same rate card and environment, no re-provisioning
- Small admin fee of $1,250 to cover reserved capacity (one-time)
- KPI milestone: final verification run and sample set validated (we’ll use your attached metrics template if you send it)

Option B — Credit top-up (token credit convertible)
- $6,000 token top-up applied immediately to your pilot account
- Convertible: if you sign a committed Dedicated or Hosted contract within 60 days, $3,000 of that top-up can be credited toward first-month committed usage (not available for one-off credits)
- No admin fee; tokens expire 90 days from issue

I’ve attached our latest pilot ratecard (redwood-pilot-ratecard.pdf) and can whip up a short SOW if you pick an option. If you want, we can also do a 30-minute sync with the integration lead to confirm the exact resources your team will need during the extension.

Which path would you prefer?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales

Subject: Fwd: PoC wrap & ask: quick extension or top-up? (internal pricing ask)

Team — forwarding Sara’s note. Quick internal calc:
- Option A margin: admin fee $1,250 covers 3-week reserved slot; estimated incremental cost ~$700 (GPU footprint + infra ops) -> ~44% gross margin, keeps customer in our hosted sandbox and simplifies conversion path.
- Option B margin: $6k credit, convertible $3k -> if customer converts, we effectively reduce first-month ARPA by $3k but likely accelerate commit. Top-up tokens expire 90d -> higher short-term cashless exposure.

My recommendation: offer both, but sweeten Option A to reduce friction:
- Offer a 2-week complimentary extension + 1 optional week at $800 (instead of $1,250 admin fee). That gets them the time they need, reduces cover cost, and incentivizes conversion during the extension.
- Keep Option B as $6k token top-up with the $3k conversion credit (standard).

Laura/Priyom — can you confirm we’re OK with the 2-week complimentary + pay-for-week approach (sits in our pilot playbook as an approved exception up to $1k waive)? If yes I’ll send the SOW and DocuSign. I attached internal-pricing-backcalc.xlsx for your review.

Karthik
